newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine banks may shut Aug30 to prepare for hryvna.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine banks may shut Aug30 to prepare for hryvna.

text.p: Ukrainian banks may close on Friday to prepare for the introduction of Ukraine's new hryvna currency, a senior central bank official said on Wednesday.

"The banks have a lot of work to do with their accounts prior to the introduction on September 2, because as of that day all transactions will be done with the hryvna," said National Bank of Ukraine deputy chairman Volodymyr Bondar.
"It's not certain that the banks would be working on Friday," he said. The central bank will decide on the matter by the end of the week, he said.
If banks close, the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange will also be closed, he added.
Ukraine's interim karbovanets currency was unchanged at 176,100 to the dollar on the exchange on Wednesday, the rate in effect since August 8.
The announcement of the new currency has not affected the karbovanets on the exchange or in the interbank market.
But it dropped to 250,000 against the dollar in some parts of Ukraine immediately before Sunday's announcement.
The hryvna will be introduced on September 2 and the karbovanets withdrawn by September 16.
Bondar said the value of the hryvna, which has been set at 100,000 karbovanets, would not be affected if the exchange closes on Friday.
"We're satisfied that everything is going according to plan, and there are no notable changes in the value of the karbovanets against the dollar," he said.
"The National Bank can reconcile, with little effort, any changes in supply and demand on the exchange." --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
